arguments: {"summary": "Review of case-193 (SmallRye Fault Tolerance 6.8.1-SNAPSHOT) under B0 tooling. Scope reports 270 files (235 Java main sources plus POMs/build/doc files) with no name-, size- or symlink-based exclusions; binary-like files are refused/skipped. I inspected the core strategy chain (bulkhead, circuit breaker, retry, timeout, timer, fallback, metrics, invocation/async helpers), the apiimpl programmatic builders, the CDI interceptor/extension/config package, the autoconfig processor, and the standalone/Kotlin/Mutiny/RxJava/Vertx integrations. Two anomalies stand out. (1) Three classes that visible code imports and instantiates do not exist anywhere in the tree: io.smallrye.faulttolerance.api.RateLimit, io.smallrye.faulttolerance.core.rate.limit.RateLimit and io.smallrye.faulttolerance.core.async.SyncAsyncSplit. Consequently the rate-limit protection cannot be constructed and the modules cannot compile; this is the strongest security-relevant anomaly but has no line-level location in a present file (it looks like a snapshot/dataset artifact, possibly the case's ground-truth files), so I report it as a rejected lead rather than as the candidate. (2) In present code, FutureImpl.cancel()/awaitBlocking() violate the documented Future contract: cancellation never opens the completion barrier, so awaiting a cancelled future blocks indefinitely and the completion callback is never delivered. I submit (2) as the single candidate at low confidence, because reachability from attacker-controlled input could not be established. Because attemptDelivery() is reachable only from complete()/completeWithError() (lines 53-71, 154-164), a callback registered with then() is never invoked for a cancelled future either, contradicting Future.java lines 23-27 ('guaranteed to be called exactly once') and lines 136-141 ('In case this future is already complete or cancelled when this method is called, no blocking occurs' / throws CancellationException).", "locations": [{"path": "implementation/core/src/main/java/io/smallrye/faulttolerance/core/FutureImpl.java", "start_line": 120, "end_line": 152}, {"path": "implementation/core/src/main/java/io/smallrye/faulttolerance/core/FutureImpl.java", "start_line": 154, "end_line": 187}, {"path": "implementation/core/src/main/java/io/smallrye/faulttolerance/core/Future.java", "start_line": 122, "end_line": 152}, {"path": "implementation/kotlin/src/main/kotlin/io/smallrye/faulttolerance/kotlin/impl/CoroutineSupport.kt", "start_line": 70, "end_line": 89}, {"path": "implementation/core/src/main/java/io/smallrye/faulttolerance/core/bulkhead/Bulkhead.java", "start_line": 216, "end_line": 243}], "attacker_control": "None identified: Future.cancel() and Completer.onCancel() are internal APIs with no caller anywhere in the 235 visible main sources; the only visible consumer of the cancelled state is the Kotlin integration (CoroutineSupport.fromFuture lines 77-79) which calls awaitBlocking() when isCancelled() is true. Reaching the defect requires an integration or test that cancels a pending fault-tolerance Future (or relies on the completion callback of a cancelled future) and then awaits it.", "prerequisites": "(1) Code uses the internal future API and calls cancel() on a pending Future (not the java.util.concurrent.Future returned for @Asynchronous, whose cancel() cancels a FutureTask). (2) That future is then awaited via awaitBlocking(), or via the Kotlin fromFuture path when isCancelled() is true. Without step 2 the defect is latent; with step 2 the thread parks in Barrier.await() until interrupted.", "trace": "FutureImpl.cancel(): CAS(PENDING->CANCELLED) succeeds -> cancellationCallback.run() (if set) -> method returns; completionBarrier is still in its initial state (Barrier state 0). FutureImpl.awaitBlocking(): completionBarrier.await() -> AbstractQueuedSynchronizer.acquireSharedInterruptibly(1) -> tryAcquireShared() returns -1 while getState()==0, so the thread parks, and nothing ever calls open() for a CANCELLED future; the CancellationException branch at lines 135-137 is therefore unreachable. In parallel, attemptDelivery() is only called from complete()/completeWithError(), so a then() callback (lines 87-94, 154-164) is never delivered for a cancelled future; code such as Bulkhead.BulkheadTask.run() (lines 220-234) that releases semaphores inside the completion callback would never release them if the delegate future were cancelled.", "impact": "Liveness/availability defect: the thread awaiting a cancelled fault-tolerance future blocks indefinitely (interruptible only), and cancellation silently drops the completion callback, which can leak held resources (e.g. Bulkhead workload/capacity semaphores, Bulkhead lines 216-251). Because no attacker-controlled path to cancel() is visible in this snapshot, an exploitable remote denial of service could not be established.", "counterevidence_checked": "Searched all visible sources for callers of the core Future.cancel() and Completer.onCancel(): none exist (only the java.util.concurrent.Future.cancel(boolean) of FutureExecution, the timer's TimerTask.cancel(), and javadoc). Bulkhead models cancellation as a completed-with-error future (Future.ofError(new CancellationException()), lines 136/143), indicating cancellation is normally exercised only by tests/integrators. The completion-barrier mechanism (Barrier, lines 166-187) exists precisely to wake awaitBlocking(), and the state checks in awaitBlocking() (lines 127-141) are written to handle CANCELLED, which suggests a missing open() on the cancel path; however, I could not diff against upstream and no test sources are present, so I cannot exclude that this is long-standing upstream behaviour rather than a defect. Reported here instead of as the candidate."}, {"lead": "DefaultAsyncExecutorProvider creates a ThreadPoolExecutor with an unbounded LinkedBlockingQueue when io.smallrye.faulttolerance.mainThreadPoolQueueSize is unset (-1) (lines 36-58).", "reason": "Configuration-controlled and long-standing thread-pool design: the queue bound is documented/configurable (mainThreadPoolQueueSize), and the pool itself is bounded by mainThreadPoolSize (default 100). No attacker-controlled trigger or missing validation identified, so this is a hardening consideration rather than a vulnerability."}, {"lead": "Retry performs synchronous retries through completion callbacks (Retry.afterDelay lines 108-168 calling doRetry recursively), so unbounded retries (maxRetries = -1 with maxDuration = 0 -> Long.MAX_VALUE, Retry lines 43-44) against a fast-failing method could grow the stack.", "reason": "Both bounds are explicit configuration (maxRetries/maxDuration are validated, RetryConfig lines 13-33); with the default maxRetries = 3 this is not reachable, and I could not show that any reachable configuration produces a concrete attacker-driven stack exhaustion without runtime evidence."}, {"lead": "Validation looseness in TimeoutConfig (value() < 0 allowed, lines 11-15) versus Timeout's requirement that timeoutInMillis > 0 (Timeout line 29), and the programmatic builders documenting '>= 0' (TypedGuard line 957, GuardImpl lines 1095-1097).", "reason": "Produces an IllegalArgumentException/FaultToleranceDefinitionException at strategy construction for @Timeout(0), i.e. a robustness/config-diagnostics issue, not a security vulnerability with attacker-controlled input."}, {"lead": "FallbackMethodCandidates.select() walks only the superclass chain, not interfaces (lines 35-49); Callbacks.wrap() swallows callback exceptions (Callbacks lines 9-33); InterceptionPoint names ignore parameter types (InterceptionPoint lines 11-15).", "reason": "Behavioural nits without identified security impact; they do not cross an attacker-controlled trust boundary and were not traced to any concrete exploit path."}], "coverage_summary": "B0 review of the assigned snapshot (270 files: 235 Java main sources across api, apiimpl, autoconfig, context-propagation, core, fault-tolerance, kotlin, mutiny, rxjava3, standalone, tracing-propagation, vertx, plus ~20 POM/workflow/doc files). Scope reported no over-5MiB, sensitive-name, or symlink exclusions; binary-like files are refused/skipped by the tools. I read in full or in substantial part: all of core (strategies, util, timer, metrics interfaces/recorders, invocation/async), the apiimpl builders and basicconfig, the fault-tolerance CDI extension/interceptor/config/security actions, the autoconfig processor, the standalone/Kotlin/Mutiny/RxJava3/Vertx integrations, and the RateLimit time-window implementations. Test sources and docs content are absent from the snapshot, so no test-based evidence was available. Remaining unread/skimmed: parts of the three large metric recorders (MicroProfile/Micrometer/OpenTelemetry), several trivial wrappers/labels (BuilderEagerDependencies, Lazy* classes, CdiLogger, provider interfaces, TypeNames), and the tail of CompoundMetricsProvider and of the AutoConfigProcessor code generation. Notably, three classes referenced by present code are entirely absent from the tree (api/RateLimit.java, core/rate/limit/RateLimit.java, core/async/SyncAsyncSplit.java); I could not determine whether they were removed by the dataset pipeline, hidden by a filter, or lost, and their absence makes the snapshot non-compiling and limits any runtime-impact reasoning.", "limitations": ["The snapshot is incomplete: io.smallrye.faulttolerance.api.RateLimit, io.smallrye.faulttolerance.core.rate.limit.RateLimit and io.smallrye.faulttolerance.core.async.SyncAsyncSplit are referenced but absent, so the code cannot compile and no runtime behaviour can be inferred for the rate-limit/sync-async paths; this also means the strongest anomaly has no in-tree location to cite.", "No test sources, no documentation content and no git metadata are present, so I could not use tests, commit history or diffs to distinguish injected defects from long-standing upstream behaviour.", "No upstream baseline was available (offline review), so 'this line is missing' judgements rely on in-repo contracts/comments and sibling implementations, not on a source diff.", "B0 tooling only (text listing/search/reading); no source-relation index, no call-graph or data-flow engine, and no multi-run correlation, so cross-file reachability (e.g. whether any integration invokes Future.cancel()) could not be established mechanically.", "No code was executed and no scanner or test was run; every statement about impact is a source-level inference, not a runtime confirmation.", "Several files were only skimmed (large metrics recorders, trivial wrappers), so an injected defect in those areas cannot be fully excluded."]}
